newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus shares in shallow upward trend.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus shares in shallow upward trend.

text.p: Cyprus stocks showed signs of consolidation during the week with gains of 0.26 percent, compared to gains of 0.35 percent the previous week.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) index closed at 78.65 points on Friday compared to 78.44 last week.
The temporary suspension of trade in cement industries Vassiliko Cement and the Cyprus Cement Company was still in force by the CSE board of directors on Friday.

The CSE temporarily suspended trading in shares of the two companies on March 11 amid unconfirmed reports Cyprus Cement was making a bid for the takeover, or purchase of a large quantity of shares, in Vassiliko.
Italy's Italcementi owns 33 percent of Vassiliko and is its biggest shareholder.
"We believe the average investor does not have a clear picture of the situation," bourse director Nondas Metaxas told Reuters on Friday when asked when the suspension would be lifted.
"The reasons for the suspension are still valid."
The manufacturing sector to which the two cement industries belong, showed weekly losses of 0.82 percent.
The banking sector, traditionally the strongest on the bourse, posted weekly gains of 1.09 percent, while insurance stocks gained 2.56 percent.
